For "anti-aging" and more energy: what is sold, what the evidence says, and what is not even a peptide.

No peptide is approved for aging or energy. The ones sold for it were reviewed by an FDA advisory committee in July 2026, and the FDA proposed keeping them off the compounding list.

  • EpitalonNot approved; FDA proposed excluding it from compounding (Jul 2026)A short peptide sold as an anti-aging shot, with thin and old human evidence.

    A four-amino-acid peptide sold as an "anti-aging" shot; human evidence is thin and old. Reviewed by the FDA in July 2026; proposed exclusion. 6

    Not approved.

    Research-use shops.

  • MOTS-cNot approved; FDA proposed excluding it from compounding (Jul 2026)A peptide sold for energy, tested in animals only.

    A "mitochondrial" peptide sold for energy; animal studies only. Same July 2026 review. 6

    Not approved.

    Research-use shops.

  • NAD+ injectionsNot a peptide; compounded, not FDA approvedNot a peptideNot a peptide: a vitamin-B3-derived molecule that clinics sell as shots or drips.

    Not a peptide: a vitamin-B3-derived molecule sold by clinics as shots or drips for energy.

    Not FDA approved.

    Clinics and compounding pharmacies.

What is approved instead: Longevity peptides: Epitalon, MOTS-c and NAD+ in 2026
